chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Udaym ibn al-Hurr, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who sees in her sleep what a man sees: is ghusl obligatory upon her? He said: "Yes, and do not tell them, lest they take it as a pretext."

key_terms.اَلْمَرْأَةِ: the woman being asked about in the legal ruling
key_terms.تُحَدِّثُوهُنَّ: informing or telling them about this matter
key_terms.عِلَّةً: a pretext or excuse used to justify something
key_terms.نَعَمْ: an affirmative answer establishing the ruling

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have to perform ghusl if she experiences a sexual dream?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that ghusl becomes obligatory for a woman if she experiences in sleep what causes the same ruling for a man. It also includes an instruction not to publicize this to women in a way that would lead some to use it as an excuse or pretext.
